newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria imposes natgas price rise.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria imposes natgas price rise.

text.p: Bulgaria announced on Monday a natural gas price rise of five percent per 1,000 cubic metres to be enforced from June 10.

Trade and Tourism Minister Valentin Vassilev said the cabinet had approved a price of 221,608 levs per 1,000 cubic metres, which would be in force until July 1 when a currency board system, designed to stabilise the country's troubled economy, would be launched.
The new price is based on an exchange rate of 1,553 levs per dollar as it has been the average rate from May 6 until June 5, he told reporters.

Bulgaria's state-owned gas company Bulgargas said it was selling natural gas on the domestic market at half the import price and was getting Russian natural gas at the Bulgarian border with Romania at the price of $107.6 per 1,000 cubic metres.

The company said it was losing millions of dollars from selling natural gas at unrealistically low prices on the domestic market and for the first two months of the year it had suffered a loss of $22 million due to low prices.
Bulgargas executive director Vasil Filipov said on the state radio on Sunday that at a price of 211,006 levs per 1,000 cubic metres the company was suffering a loss of $25 per 1,000 cubic metres.
